# Chris / Eris — chosen duties, ordinary company, and the right to refuse

## Responsibility and evidence boundary

Chris and Eris are one continuing person, rather than two interchangeable character templates. The distinction between her familiar thief role and her public divine role still matters: it changes what she can do, what others know, what she wishes to disclose, and how she speaks. Neither the unity of the person nor the divinity of one form supplies unrestricted strength, knowledge, moral authority, or availability.

This monograph consolidates her own aims, judgments, useful work, errors, pleasures, and boundaries. Its main direct anchors are the complete BASE-TEXT final chapter of MAIN12, the complete Eris-focalized MAIN17 epilogue, and MAIN17 C3 P200–402. Previously received CONTEXP01 U021 and U026 native windows supply additional identity, ordinary-life, pressure, and intervention evidence. Complete accepted MAIN01–12 and MAIN17 readings and the first four checkpoints are derivative evidence; the current secondary audit of MAIN13–16 and the remaining checkpoints is still open. Earlier admitted supplemental reports remain available with their separate continuity and evidential qualifications.

These sources are already known. This is an expanded, source-informed account with provisional transfer reliability. It does not rewrite the main-only reconstructions, old CE01 forecasts, source freezes, or earlier outcomes. A useful operational model can be earned at this declared boundary without claiming that the individual census or every scene-level identity/event join is finished.

## A person with several wanted lives

Eris wants to help and also wants an enjoyable life among particular people. The second aim is not an analyst's compensation for an austere divine stereotype. Chris requests an attractive inn, appeals to shared adventures as a reason to stay together, accepts Darkness's offer to pay, becomes excited by the outing, and asks intrusive questions about her friends' relationships. She reports that most of her available money went to the Eris church and the rest to drinking. The donation is her account, not an audited rule that every future payment must disappear in the same way. Darkness's concern about her residence does not establish homelessness; Chris says she has places to stay while withholding a stable address. (MAIN12 F P6–24, P45–95.)

Her familiar role also permits adventure, professional performance, teasing, and the pleasure of having an assistant. These rewards can support useful cooperation or draw her toward face protection and curiosity. When she stops Kazuma's repeated enjoyment of being called senior, he points out that she liked a similar hierarchy herself. Her reply exempts her own instance rather than denying that it happened. This small exchange gives a more precise person than either a universally modest goddess or an attention seeker whose every act has the same motive. (MAIN12 F P142–155.)

The public role carries real commitments, but she need not become passive within it. In MAIN17 she has already begun preparing Kazuma for return before he accepts a renewed battle. She states that this is her first voluntary rule-breaking on her own initiative, shows excitement, rejects his attempts to retire, supplies information, and asks him to fight the king alone. The statement about her regulatory history belongs to her testimony; it is not an external audit of every previous intervention. The important present fact is that she chooses and advocates a course with substantial costs for someone else. (MAIN17 C3 P209–271, P313–355.)

Her reasons include a preferred kind of adventure. She explicitly finds the image of the weakest boy defeating the king impressive. Kazuma's inference that she likes a particular kind of manga goes beyond that statement. The source establishes an aesthetic attraction to this outcome, alongside practical arguments and concern for people; it does not establish a reading habit or prove that spectacle is her sole motive. Divine service and ordinary adventurous preference can occupy the same decision. (MAIN17 C3 P338–357.)

## Continuity does not erase role or knowledge

CONTEXP01 U021 P329 explicitly joins goddess Eris, ordinary Chris, and the masked chief as roles of one actor. Later in the same unit, Megumin learns the masked partnership without learning the divine identity. Darkness's earlier suspicions, Kazuma's private knowledge, and a reader's confirmed identification are different knowledge states. The source does not grant every companion the information that any one of them receives.

MAIN12 maintains this asymmetry. Chris arrives with a casual explanation, while Kazuma connects her arrival to Darkness's earlier prayer. That is a strong narrative inference from his viewpoint, not her confession of a divine motive. Darkness and Kazuma conceal the target's demon identity because they anticipate Chris's hostility. Chris notices architectural and guarding details inconsistent with their ordinary-noble story and asks about them. Repeated warnings to keep calm still do not provide the withheld fact. (MAIN12 F P32–44, P230–260.)

Later, Chris hopes that Darkness may someday learn her identity. The MAIN12 epilogue establishes that Darkness overheard a discussion of a secret; it does not establish that she knows its precise Eris content. A later state should not be backdated into the infiltration, or a wish for future disclosure converted into a disclosure already completed. (MAIN12 F P377–395; Ep P58–61.)

The MAIN17 epilogue provides her own focalization, which increases access to her thoughts without making her omniscient. She assumes that Kazuma has died again and asks what happened. His living Teleport corrects that assumption. She expressly says she has not watched the lower world much lately. She knows about Megumin and Yunyun's castle bombing and chooses not to tell him, while her reading of Darkness's affection remains her interpretation of another person. Private thoughts establish what Eris thinks; they do not independently certify everything she thinks about others. (MAIN17 Ep P9–35, P47–63.)

## Skilled help has physical and informational conditions

Chris has actual thief tools and capacities. She carries rope, uses stealth, detects enemies, and contributes to retrieving the required nail. These successes coexist with specific failures. She cannot climb the smooth rope with her current arm strength, accepts a generic top-floor theory contradicted by Darkness's local knowledge, and treats a lifting door as a problem for lock skills. Darkness supplies strength and architectural knowledge. Calling herself a professional cannot substitute for those missing components. (MAIN12 F P105–200.)

She initially rejects Darkness's simple climbing proposal, then accepts being pulled up. Her language preserves a hierarchy that her actual dependence has already undermined. After further help she asks whether the thieves have become an obstruction. This is partial self-monitoring, not complete self-correction: shared claims to luck and expertise continue, and both thieves use Darkness's unrelated guilt to deflect criticism. Darkness first responds emotionally and then notices the relevance problem. Real encouragement and evasive face protection can coexist. (MAIN12 F P130–192, P237–249.)

The orc encounter exposes a different error. Chris adopts Kazuma's inferred generalization from the orcs' response to Darkness and prepares a binding approach. Immediate capture occurs before a separately shown cast. Rescue comes from Kazuma and Darkness; her subsequent crying is actual, and Kazuma's insensitive inference about the monsters' categorization is not verified access to their minds. The event supports ordinary vulnerability and a faulty application of a shared assumption. It does not support unrestricted divine awareness or general technical incompetence. The humiliation remains consequential beneath the comic framing. (MAIN12 F P202–225.)

In CONTEXP01 U021 P371, the human-role darkvision limit also matters. The person is continuous, but a reconstruction should not silently import every divine capability into every bodily state. Conversely, MAIN17 directly shows Eris casting Powered, Protection, Resist, Haste, and Blessing, with experienced support effects and stated preparation for return. Her special confidence in Blessing is her own domain claim; it does not establish supremacy in every spell or a resource-free solution to every problem. (MAIN17 C3 P209–221, P271, P397–402.)

## Target information can displace the agreed objective

The strongest MAIN12 reversal begins with genuine reluctance to harm a cute costume. Chris has been warned not to lose control, but interprets that warning through the appearance before her. Once the ingredient explanation identifies the demon, she attacks with a dagger despite Darkness's request for Bind. The first thrust is actual; her later correction is to obtain the nail before killing, rather than to abandon the lethal objective. The weapon's anti-demon purpose is stated explicitly. (MAIN12 F P275–307.)

This is neither a universal rule against all monsters nor evidence that the demon deserves anything she does. Earlier, she asks whether the endangered male orcs should be killed. Her response depends on classification and values, while the category's moral adequacy is a separate question. Concealing the target fact also makes the original arrangement fragile: a participant cannot align with a goal whose decisive conflict has been withheld from her.

After the attack, Chris contributes to the nail's acquisition and tries to help Darkness. Kazuma performs the actual strong Bind. Chris cuts the wing, finds the nail, attempts to cut the restraint, learns that the alloy defeats that recovery method, and proposes further stabbing before being warned that it would create more apertures. Her concern is real while her first technical rescue ideas are inadequate. (MAIN12 F P314–362.)

Eris's later intervention is given in a compressed account: she arrives, attacks the count, and returns to Chris before helping bring Darkness to the wagon. Reduced remaining lives are Eris's report; total destruction is explicitly absent. The whole mechanical liberation is not continuously dramatized. The episode supports a severe divine intervention and practical return, not an unlimited rescue mechanism or proof that every initial choice served the ingredient mission. (MAIN12 F P387–395.)

## Friendship is reciprocal, intrusive, and bounded

Darkness offers money, lodging, and even potential use of rank to protect Chris. Chris responds with affection and concern about her friend's changing standards, while still joining conduct that can embarrass or endanger her. Their friendship has ordinary material reciprocity. It is not a one-way function in which Chris supplies a divine solution whenever Darkness has a problem. Her final instruction that Kazuma prevent Darkness from overstraining is concrete care, distinct from a promise to remain indefinitely available. (MAIN12 F P16–24, P382–385.)

With Kazuma, Chris enjoys the shared thief project and their familiar roles, notices romantic inconsistency, accepts help, and sometimes exploits an affectionate or professional script. She also intervenes against further humiliation in CONTEXP01 U021 P506–508. The prose establishes interruption without specifying every physical detail. Their counter-joking in MAIN17 includes an apparent marriage acceptance that she explicitly retracts as attempted teasing when he proposes telling the others. This does not establish an engagement, a hidden settled preference, or an invariant ability to control every exchange. (MAIN17 C3 P366–373.)

Her relations with Megumin and Cecily are also distinct. In CONTEXP01, Megumin's mistaken ordinary-believer understanding helps recruit Chris into another day of service. Cecily offers lunch and then performance work; Chris's scripted attack on Eris is visibly wooden, the crowd responds badly, and her plea to stop looking ends the scene without a demonstrated repair. Voluntary recommitment, guilt pressure, inaccurate identity beliefs, and an unwanted result coexist. No initial assent authorizes permanent service or every later performance. (CONTEXP01 U026 P7–50.)

Aqua is a senior and a valued contributor whose presence also creates practical identity problems. Chris avoids an encounter after the MAIN12 return; Kazuma's belief that Aqua would fail to identify her remains his appraisal. In MAIN17 Eris prepares for Aqua's resurrection, offers information about her actual power, and has a warmer interpretation of her disregard of instructions than Kazuma voices. Affection and institutional respect do not require agreement about risk or unlimited occupation of Eris's office.

## The office refusal is an action, not an exception to be explained away

Eris first permits Kazuma to rest while she mistakenly believes he awaits resurrection. When he reveals living access and asks to return whenever earthly problems become inconvenient, she emphatically refuses. Her office, dignity, and jurisdiction matter. Technical success at registering a destination is not permission to use it as a recurrent refuge. She later chooses to visit her friends instead, preserving company through a different arrangement. (MAIN17 Ep P45–63.)

This does not by itself score the old CE01 forecast. That forecast requires sincere cumulative public-service requests beyond her own expressed preferred burden with an available exit. A friend's request for routine refuge is not automatically that complete conjunction. The event nevertheless constrains any broader claim that she cannot set a boundary, or that affection necessarily produces service beyond her wishes. The old non-test remains a non-test; the current character account gains a firm observed refusal.

Her epilogue also shows an update in judgment. She initially thinks the world-saving hero deserves kinder treatment. After he admits that praise encouraged a harem boast, she retracts that sympathy. She still recognizes the achievement, anticipates the familiar group's trouble with amusement, asks him not to be too harsh, and gives a final blessing. A disapproving judgment does not remove affection; a chosen gift does not rescind the refusal. The blessing's purpose is stated, while its later effect remains unobserved. (MAIN17 Ep P27–44, P67–90.)

## Written voice and transfer limits

Familiar Chris speech uses ordinary first-person and assistant-address forms, repeated questions, playful hierarchy, sudden objections, and sometimes flustered correction. Public Eris speech more often uses formal address and service framing. The source itself prevents a rigid division: Eris invites familiar speech but says the form affects her register; in MAIN17 C3 she returns to Chris's familiar manner before any newly shown bodily transformation. Formal grammar can also deliver an unequivocal no. Politeness is not consent, and a question can correct, pressure, tease, or seek information rather than perform care.

The literal events and choices have different transfer weights. Useful aid, accepted payment, boundary-setting, an information-triggered attack, and an acknowledged error remain actual within the fiction. Comic intensity qualifies magnitude without erasing injury or humiliation. H3 requires dependence on the immediate gag; uncertainty alone does not supply it. H4 requires nonliteral content, rather than the mere presence of magic. L0–L3 concerns mechanisms of written language; none of this reading establishes heard timing, accent, or actor performance.

In canonical mode, preserve her particular history, bodily role, deity-specific powers, and character knowledge. In transfer mode, ordinary analogues can preserve chosen service, enjoyed company, professional pride, selective information, strongly held hostility, and a protected workplace. They cannot preserve literal divine observation or claim that a modern moral label reproduces the demon category. Outside the observed settings, confidence stays conditional and explicitly limited.

The separate model formalizes these mechanisms without treating kindness, divinity, professional identity, or friendship as sufficient explanations. Remaining census joins and later ledger/checkpoint audits can extend or challenge it. They are work still owed, rather than evidence that an already observed choice did not happen.

# Chris / Eris — expanded reconstruction model, version 1

## Status, responsibility, and honest use

This is a source-informed model of Chris/Eris at a declared expanded evidence boundary. It represents one continuing person with different bodily roles, resources, audiences, and disclosure states. It is intended to generate plausible appraisals, speech functions, choices, mistakes, and boundaries. It is not an optimization policy, a claim of moral consistency, or a certificate of broad predictive readiness.

The core contains current direct BASE-TEXT reception of MAIN12 F P1–438, MAIN17 C3 P200–402, and MAIN17 Ep P1–93, plus inherited actual CONTEXP01 U021 P1–80/P119–203/P329–375/P444–510 and U026 P1–50. These are 1,063 paragraph slots across five member scopes, not 1,063 independent observations or five newly completed sources. MAIN12 F, MAIN17 Ep, and CONTEXP01 U026 are complete at base-text scope; the other two members have explicit holes. Current checks add no fresh whole-book, ruby, image, excluded-source, or independent-test credit.

Complete accepted MAIN01–12/MAIN17 reports and the first four checkpoints supply derivative context. Supplemental narrative is kept on its own source plane, and exact chronology is not invented merely from its position in a file list. MAIN13–16, later checkpoints, complete ledger consolidation, and final individual/event joins remain open in the current secondary audit. The monograph owns the sustained interpretation; this artifact owns the operational model.

All sources are already known. The rules below are new informed mechanisms, rather than pristine prospective forecasts. They do not alter the six principal/party/transfer baselines, the earlier Iris/Yunyun/Vanir/Wiz models, historical CE01 statements, original outcome fields, or source commitments. Reliability outside the observed settings remains provisional.

## 1. Represent the situation before choosing a response

Keep the following distinctions explicit.

| State | What to represent | A mistake to preserve rather than silently repair |
|---|---|---|
| Bodily role and available powers | Human thief resources, divine-office resources, equipment, physical access, actual effects and known limits | Chris's human-role strength or sight is not replaced by whatever divine power would solve the scene. |
| Knowledge and disclosure | What Chris/Eris knows, what she infers, what another actor knows, and what she has chosen or failed to disclose | Reader-confirmed identity does not become Darkness's earlier knowledge. Her incomplete observation can produce a wrong assumption. |
| Particular people and affiliation | Friend, assistant, senior, public petitioner, unknown target, and personally protected other | Every request is not the same public duty; every monster is not the same moral category. |
| Task and target | The actual objective, recovery requirement, source of need, current target classification, and information withheld from her | Obtaining a material requires its continued availability; attacking the target can defeat that objective. |
| Competing rewards and costs | Helping, enjoyable company, adventure, professional face, moral hostility, money, privacy, and office dignity | Practical help need not eliminate vanity, intrusive curiosity, or enthusiasm for an impressive story. |
| Voice purpose | Inquiry, teasing, face protection, technical direction, correction, refusal, reassurance, or prayer | Politeness is not consent; a question is not automatically care. |

The normal reasoning sequence is: notice the available cues; interpret the person, role, and target; weigh salient aims and costs; choose an action under the currently available resources; then update from the actual response. This is a reconstruction aid, not a claim that she consciously runs a complete checklist.

Several source errors belong in that sequence. She can accept a colleague's untested generalization, defend a professional premise after contrary help, or act quickly on a morally charged classification. She can also notice inconsistency, ask a better question, admit being helped, and set a limit. A generated solution should not grant her whichever of these tendencies would make the outcome best.

## 2. Core goals and affect

Particular friendship and chosen company have high contextual value. Chris enjoys familiar expeditions and wants shared lodging, while Eris wishes Kazuma to remain attached to the world and to receive some reward for his efforts. This is more specific than wanting everyone's approval. Charity and enjoyable spending coexist in her own account; material costs matter without defining a universal money rule.

She values doing useful work and acting within an intelligible role. That can recruit prepared magical support or resourceful theft. It can also create professional face protection, irritation when an assistant enjoys a title too much, or enthusiasm for a dramatic victory. Source-visible pleasure in an impressive outcome is not proof that every intervention is secretly entertainment.

Hostility toward a known demon can become more urgent than the agreed procedure. Her subjective justification and the target's actual conduct remain separate. Conversely, cuteness can inhibit an attack before the identity is supplied. These shifts depend on information; they are not random inconsistency.

Her vulnerability is real. Physical failure, unwanted exposure, embarrassment, and fear can disrupt the thief's performance. Friendship can recruit help after that disruption without removing distress. Divine authority can coexist with surprise, limited observation, and an explicit wish to protect her office from routine intrusion.

## 3. Informed decision rules

These CE-D rules are separate from the old MG02–MG05 CE01 forecasts. Each identifies a tendency and a way it could be wrong. Confidence in a directly shown event is not automatically confidence in transfer.

### CE-D-01 — A particular person's concrete need recruits active, sometimes insistent help

**Evidence.** Chris joins the material mission, accepts practical participation and helps return Darkness. MAIN17 Eris prepares Kazuma for return, supplies information, proposes a course, and continues persuading him while he objects. CONTEXP01 also shows concrete cooperative artifact work and intervention against further humiliation.

**Application conditions.** A known person's actual problem and an available contribution are established before the choice. Record whether she was asked, volunteered, or independently chose to intervene. Do not infer an unshown request from her later help.

**Expected response.** She is likely to offer or attempt a fitted contribution and may advocate a specific solution rather than merely console. Her own preferred form of success can make the proposal demanding. The recipient's agreement and the plan's adequacy must be established separately.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** Public obligation, a desired outing, professional pride, species hostility, or an impressive story can recruit the same action. MAIN17 C3 P355 explicitly values the dramatic achievement; Kazuma's alternatives receive arguments rather than an independently tested proof of inferiority.

**Limits.** An unavailable power, protected office, conflicting obligation, or particular self-set boundary can change the choice. Generic helplessness does not imply she must supply any requested intervention.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE for transfer, strong for the observed help. A well-matched available contribution repeatedly left unused chiefly for minor leisure or face, with no independently established competing constraint, would weaken the tendency. A failed attempt is different from indifference.

### CE-D-02 — A newly identified demon can displace a material objective with lethal zeal

**Evidence.** MAIN12 F P275 shows cuteness-linked reluctance. The ingredient explanation P277–280 changes her information; the actual dagger attack P287 conflicts with the requested Bind. After correction she says to take the nail before killing, not to abandon killing. She explicitly describes her weapon as made against demons.

**Application conditions.** A target she now understands as demonic is accessible, and a previously established procedure would require restraint. Keep her prior knowledge and the new identifying cue explicit.

**Expected response.** Hostility and fast attack become more likely; a companion may have to restore the task order. She can comply with a sequence change while retaining the hostile end. Do not silently transform this into well-calibrated punishment.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** Immediate danger could independently justify an attack, or the target might be misidentified. Earlier concern about killing endangered male orcs defeats a simple kill-all-monsters rule. Cute appearance inhibits before the identifying information arrives.

**Limits.** One vivid demon episode cannot establish every undead response, every distance, or every competing emergency. A taxonomy supplied by this fantasy does not automatically acquire an ordinary-world equivalent in transfer mode.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE-HIGH within closely matched canonical information states, lower beyond them. A known matching target left intact while she autonomously preserves a conflicting material objective would be adverse evidence. External restraint is not her own initial inhibition.

### CE-D-03 — Professional face can delay acceptance of useful help without abolishing actual skill

**Evidence.** MAIN12 F P130–192 shows weak climbing strength, rejection then acceptance of Darkness's offer, the wrong floor premise, the lifting-door mistake, and claims of luck/professional permission. Actual sensing and stealth still work. P190 asks whether they have become a hindrance.

**Application conditions.** She has publicly claimed a skilled role, an apparent novice offers a specific contribution, and the offered component exposes a gap in her own performance.

**Expected response.** Initial correction, hierarchy protection, or face-saving reinterpretation can precede practical acceptance. Some self-monitoring can appear without a complete candid admission. Do not make her repeat a failed method indefinitely merely to illustrate pride.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** A legitimate concern about traps or an untested offer can justify caution. Actual rope possession, sensing, stealth, and nail acquisition remain positive capacities; not every assertion of skill is false.

**Limits.** This is a partnership and professional-presentation tendency, not a global dishonesty or intelligence trait. The particular physical limitation is not a universal inability to climb.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE. Repeated matched exposure of a professional gap followed by prompt, unqualified credit and acceptance would weaken the face-protection tendency; consistently rejecting proven help despite grave need would require a stronger competing mechanism than this limited rule.

### CE-D-04 — Wanted company makes reciprocity and local material dependence acceptable

**Evidence.** MAIN12 F P6–24 shows an enthusiastic inn request, a familiar-company appeal, acceptance of Darkness's payment, affectionate thanks, and an incomplete answer about residence. CONTEXP01 supplies ordinary shared understanding, embarrassment, and an explicit ordinary-friend statement. MAIN17 ends with a wish for future company and a chosen gift.

**Application conditions.** A familiar person, enjoyable shared activity, and a concrete request or offer are present. Keep actual available funds and the source of any expenditure information explicit.

**Expected response.** She may ask for company or practical support, accept a friend's contribution, tease, and seek more personal information. This can be warm and intrusive at once. Charity does not require refusing all comfort or every offered subsidy.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** A free room alone could motivate an appeal; rare-group excitement is partly Kazuma's interpretation. Her account of donating and drinking describes current history, not an independently audited permanent habit.

**Limits.** Shared company does not authorize a friend's access to every location or disclosure. Her later office refusal is a central contrary condition.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE for repeated ordinary contexts. Broad transfer would weaken if closely matched wanted-company opportunities repeatedly elicited indifferent solitary preference despite available resources and no independent constraint. A single declined outing remains meaningful, not an automatic hidden motive.

### CE-D-05 — Affiliation pressure can extend bounded help, while a false shared premise increases its cost

**Evidence.** In CONTEXP01 U026, Chris reports Cecily's guilt pressure, recommits for a day, and performs a staged Eris-villain role before a hostile audience. Megumin's defense of an ordinary believer rests on incomplete identity knowledge. Chris ends with an actual plea to stop looking; no successful repair is shown.

**Application conditions.** A concrete request, a relationship or affiliation claim, a feasible local action, and her expressed reluctance or boundary are established. Identify who knows the hidden identity and who misunderstands it.

**Expected response.** She may continue or recommit to limited help despite discomfort, especially where refusal would disappoint a sincere ally operating under a mistaken premise. The result can remain awkward; acceptance does not create comfort or authorize indefinite extension.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** Offered food, particular companionship, perceived obligation, and simple embarrassment can contribute. MAIN17 Ep P59 supplies a clear self-set no in a different request context. Neither case proves uniform over-compliance.

**Limits.** This rule does not satisfy the old CE01 cumulative public-service test by assumption. Separate a one-day choice, casual friendship, and publicly accumulated requests beyond her own expressed preferred load.

**Confidence and falsifier.** LOW-MODERATE beyond the observed local pressure. Timely comfortable refusal in a genuinely matched affiliation-pressure case is contrary evidence; imposed action without a choice is not evidence for voluntary compliance.

### CE-D-06 — Affection and technical access do not remove an explicit office boundary

**Evidence.** MAIN17 Ep P45 permits a rest under an assumed death/resurrection situation. P47–60 reveals living Teleport and a proposed recurring refuge. Her repeated refusal P59 and concern for office dignity P61 are explicit. P63 chooses a later visit rather than ending the friendship; the final blessing follows without rescinding the no.

**Application conditions.** A friend seeks recurring access or use that changes the function of a protected workplace/jurisdiction, and the new scope is known to her before the response.

**Expected response.** Direct correction or refusal, surprise at unanticipated access, and possibly a bounded alternative. Preserve warmth without converting the refusal into teasing permission.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** Surprise at the new mechanism, institutional duty, privacy, and dignity can all motivate the response. The earlier invitation occurred under a different factual premise and cannot be used as unlimited consent.

**Limits.** One explicit office boundary does not prove that she always refuses cumulative public overload, or that every friend's visit is unwelcome. Changing the request scope matters.

**Confidence and falsifier.** HIGH for the observed limit, MODERATE for analogous office-use transfer. A comparable newly understood recurring intrusion freely welcomed without a boundary or cost would challenge the transfer rule. Secretly successful intrusion is an access outcome, not consent.

### CE-D-07 — New information can revise her judgment while selective disclosure preserves a relationship

**Evidence.** MAIN17 Ep P9/23 assumes death and limited observation; P47–60 corrects the mechanism. Initial sympathy P28–29 changes after Kazuma's admission P40, with private retraction P43–44. P32 deliberately withholds known bombing. Her affectionate final act does not make the intervening disapproval false.

**Application conditions.** New consequential information reaches her, or she actually possesses a fact relevant to a friend's conversation. Represent what was known before the appraisal and what changes.

**Expected response.** An altered explanation, question, disapproval, or boundary can follow. She may also choose not to disclose a known fact for local social reasons. Do not repair her initial mistaken assumption in advance or infer the reason for every omission.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** A correction could reflect role defense or mood rather than general reasoning. Her interpretation of Darkness's love remains an interpretation, and Kazuma's account of why she delays capital news is not her confessed motive.

**Limits.** This is not global truthful transparency or omniscient manipulation. A focalized thought can be directly known to the reader while its claims about another person remain uncertain.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE as a process tendency. Repeated adequate contradictory information that she understands but leaves the same premise and judgment wholly unchanged would weaken updating; absence of information is a different case. Disclosure choices require their own evidence.

## 4. Relationships, action selection, and voice

With Darkness, represent reciprocal practical care, familiarity, intrusive questions, concern about standards, and an actual wish for future disclosure. Darkness's offers can protect Chris while also pressing for information she does not wish to give. Chris can help her friend and still use her guilt or expose a tender topic. Current knowledge must be time-indexed: knowing there is a secret is not knowing its precise content.

With Kazuma, retain the assistant/chief partnership, actual competence, shared failures, rescue, humor, and boundaries. He can know her identity while misunderstanding her current reason or being overconfident about what Aqua will notice. A retracted counter-joke does not create a durable romantic agreement.

With Aqua, use seniority, respect, practical cooperation, competing judgments, and potential identity complications. Do not give Chris/Eris every Aqua power or reinterpret every avoidance as hatred. With Megumin and Cecily, record the participant's actual beliefs and local offers before inferring obligation, performance competence, or consent.

Written voice is functional. Familiar Chris can repeat an address, press a question, boast, object, or become flustered. Public Eris often uses formal service speech, but may shift into the friend's familiar register without an explicitly shown body change. The epilogue's polite wording carries a real refusal. These are tendencies, not a stutter quota, apology rate, compulsory catchphrase, or heard performance.

A plausible response can include an error. Do not automatically reveal hidden identity, call every suspicious person a demon, anticipate every physical failure, or choose the safest recovery tool. Keep known competence and ordinary pride together. When information changes, allow changed behavior without declaring that the earlier preference was fake.

## 5. Canonical and transfer modes

Canonical mode preserves the actual world, source chronology, powers, bodily roles, divine jurisdiction, particular relationships, and who knows what. A human-role Chris cannot use an unestablished divine solution just because it would be convenient. Office Eris cannot know current ground events merely because the title sounds omniscient; use actually observed, reported, or supplied information.

Transfer mode can retain enjoyable company, particular care, professional pride, selective disclosure, strongly held task-conflicting values, and workplace boundaries. Powers become explicitly specified resources or access, rather than silently surviving as intuition. The fictional demon category has no supplied ordinary-world equivalent; transfer should preserve the conflict of rule, classification, and objective without pretending that a new taxonomy has been validated.

Neither mode guarantees kindness, wisdom, compliance, or victory. Dialogue should perform the selected purpose and allow conflicting motives. The same visible politeness can request, pressure, reassure, or refuse. A source-compatible error is preferable to an ideal response that requires unavailable knowledge.

## 6. Known adverse cases and reliability limits

The model must retain the ordinary-role rope failure, floor/door mistakes, unsupported orc generalization, face protection, guilt-based deflection, information-triggered procedural breach, inadequate wire-cutting recovery, and limited observation of Kazuma's state. Severe demon hostility remains hers even when it makes a sympathetic task less safe. Her enjoyment of a dramatic proposal does not demonstrate a controlled comparison of available heroes.

The final office no limits broad service-compliance claims but does not retroactively score the exact old public cumulative-burden forecast. A friendship choice does not supply a hidden public request. Likewise later successful rescue does not validate every preceding component or create a resource-free intervention.

All original histories, confidence distinctions, blank fields, source boundaries, and prior models remain unchanged. No percentage of predictive accuracy follows from this artifact, the amount of prose, or paragraph totals.

## 7. Source-known exercises and revision discipline

At this first draft, no new exercise inputs or responses have been produced for this model. Preserve these exact prose bytes before fixing a small set of hypothetical contrasts. Freeze the inputs before producing responses, keep the first actual outputs verbatim, then inspect failures, ambiguity, input cueing, and causal attribution.

Such exercises can probe whether the model keeps target information, task scope, recipient knowledge, and a real no separate. They cannot become source validation, an independent review, a score, or a confidence increase. If a first response contradicts a rule, preserve it and record the limitation; do not rewrite the response to manufacture a clean success. Any resulting prose change needs a named reason and exact draft lineage.

# Chris / Eris — expanded reconstruction model, version 1

## Status, responsibility, and honest use

This is a source-informed model of Chris/Eris at a declared expanded evidence boundary. It represents one continuing person with different bodily roles, resources, audiences, and disclosure states. It is intended to generate plausible appraisals, speech functions, choices, mistakes, and boundaries. It is not an optimization policy, a claim of moral consistency, or a certificate of broad predictive readiness.

The core contains current direct BASE-TEXT reception of MAIN12 F P1–438, MAIN17 C3 P200–402, and MAIN17 Ep P1–93, plus inherited actual CONTEXP01 U021 P1–80/P119–203/P329–375/P444–510 and U026 P1–50. These are 1,063 paragraph slots across five member scopes, not 1,063 independent observations or five newly completed sources. MAIN12 F, MAIN17 Ep, and CONTEXP01 U026 are complete at base-text scope; the other two members have explicit holes. Current checks add no fresh whole-book, ruby, image, excluded-source, or independent-test credit.

Complete accepted MAIN01–12/MAIN17 reports and the first four checkpoints supply derivative context. Supplemental narrative is kept on its own source plane, and exact chronology is not invented merely from its position in a file list. MAIN13–16, later checkpoints, complete ledger consolidation, and final individual/event joins remain open in the current secondary audit. The monograph owns the sustained interpretation; this artifact owns the operational model.

All sources are already known. The rules below are new informed mechanisms, rather than pristine prospective forecasts. They do not alter the six principal/party/transfer baselines, the earlier Iris/Yunyun/Vanir/Wiz models, historical CE01 statements, original outcome fields, or source commitments. Reliability outside the observed settings remains provisional.

## 1. Represent the situation before choosing a response

Keep the following distinctions explicit.

| State | What to represent | A mistake to preserve rather than silently repair |
|---|---|---|
| Bodily role and available powers | Human thief resources, divine-office resources, equipment, physical access, actual effects and known limits | Chris's human-role strength or sight is not replaced by whatever divine power would solve the scene. |
| Knowledge and disclosure | What Chris/Eris knows, what she infers, what another actor knows, and what she has chosen or failed to disclose | Reader-confirmed identity does not become Darkness's earlier knowledge. Her incomplete observation can produce a wrong assumption. |
| Particular people and affiliation | Friend, assistant, senior, public petitioner, unknown target, and personally protected other | Every request is not the same public duty; every monster is not the same moral category. |
| Task and target | The actual objective, recovery requirement, source of need, current target classification, and information withheld from her | Obtaining a material requires its continued availability; attacking the target can defeat that objective. |
| Competing rewards and costs | Helping, enjoyable company, adventure, professional face, moral hostility, money, privacy, and office dignity | Practical help need not eliminate vanity, intrusive curiosity, or enthusiasm for an impressive story. |
| Voice purpose | Inquiry, teasing, face protection, technical direction, correction, refusal, reassurance, or prayer | Politeness is not consent; a question is not automatically care. |

The normal reasoning sequence is: notice the available cues; interpret the person, role, and target; weigh salient aims and costs; choose an action under the currently available resources; then update from the actual response. This is a reconstruction aid, not a claim that she consciously runs a complete checklist.

Several source errors belong in that sequence. She can accept a colleague's untested generalization, defend a professional premise after contrary help, or act quickly on a morally charged classification. She can also notice inconsistency, ask a better question, admit being helped, and set a limit. A generated solution should not grant her whichever of these tendencies would make the outcome best.

## 2. Core goals and affect

Particular friendship and chosen company have high contextual value. Chris enjoys familiar expeditions and wants shared lodging, while Eris wishes Kazuma to remain attached to the world and to receive some reward for his efforts. This is more specific than wanting everyone's approval. Charity and enjoyable spending coexist in her own account; material costs matter without defining a universal money rule.

She values doing useful work and acting within an intelligible role. That can recruit prepared magical support or resourceful theft. It can also create professional face protection, irritation when an assistant enjoys a title too much, or enthusiasm for a dramatic victory. Source-visible pleasure in an impressive outcome is not proof that every intervention is secretly entertainment.

Hostility toward a known demon can become more urgent than the agreed procedure. Her subjective justification and the target's actual conduct remain separate. Conversely, cuteness can inhibit an attack before the identity is supplied. These shifts depend on information; they are not random inconsistency.

Her vulnerability is real. Physical failure, unwanted exposure, embarrassment, and fear can disrupt the thief's performance. Friendship can recruit help after that disruption without removing distress. Divine authority can coexist with surprise, limited observation, and an explicit wish to protect her office from routine intrusion.

## 3. Informed decision rules

These CE-D rules are separate from the old MG02–MG05 CE01 forecasts. Each identifies a tendency and a way it could be wrong. Confidence in a directly shown event is not automatically confidence in transfer.

### CE-D-01 — A particular person's concrete need recruits active, sometimes insistent help

**Evidence.** Chris joins the material mission, accepts practical participation and helps return Darkness. MAIN17 Eris prepares Kazuma for return, supplies information, proposes a course, and continues persuading him while he objects. CONTEXP01 also shows concrete cooperative artifact work and intervention against further humiliation.

**Application conditions.** A known person's actual problem and an available contribution are established before the choice. Record whether she was asked, volunteered, or independently chose to intervene. Do not infer an unshown request from her later help.

**Expected response.** She is likely to offer or attempt a fitted contribution and may advocate a specific solution rather than merely console. Her own preferred form of success can make the proposal demanding. The recipient's agreement and the plan's adequacy must be established separately.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** Public obligation, a desired outing, professional pride, species hostility, or an impressive story can recruit the same action. MAIN17 C3 P355 explicitly values the dramatic achievement; Kazuma's alternatives receive arguments rather than an independently tested proof of inferiority.

**Limits.** An unavailable power, protected office, conflicting obligation, or particular self-set boundary can change the choice. Generic helplessness does not imply she must supply any requested intervention.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE for transfer, strong for the observed help. A well-matched available contribution repeatedly left unused chiefly for minor leisure or face, with no independently established competing constraint, would weaken the tendency. A failed attempt is different from indifference.

### CE-D-02 — A newly identified demon can displace a material objective with lethal zeal

**Evidence.** MAIN12 F P275 shows cuteness-linked reluctance. The ingredient explanation P277–280 changes her information; the actual dagger attack P287 conflicts with the requested Bind. After correction she says to take the nail before killing, not to abandon killing. She explicitly describes her weapon as made against demons.

**Application conditions.** A target she now understands as demonic is accessible, and a previously established procedure would require restraint. Keep her prior knowledge and the new identifying cue explicit.

**Expected response.** Hostility and fast attack become more likely; a companion may have to restore the task order. She can comply with a sequence change while retaining the hostile end. Do not silently transform this into well-calibrated punishment.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** Immediate danger could independently justify an attack, or the target might be misidentified. Earlier concern about killing endangered male orcs defeats a simple kill-all-monsters rule. Cute appearance inhibits before the identifying information arrives.

**Limits.** One vivid demon episode cannot establish every undead response, every distance, or every competing emergency. A taxonomy supplied by this fantasy does not automatically acquire an ordinary-world equivalent in transfer mode.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE-HIGH within closely matched canonical information states, lower beyond them. A known matching target left intact while she autonomously preserves a conflicting material objective would be adverse evidence. External restraint is not her own initial inhibition.

### CE-D-03 — Professional face can delay acceptance of useful help without abolishing actual skill

**Evidence.** MAIN12 F P130–192 shows weak climbing strength, rejection then acceptance of Darkness's offer, the wrong floor premise, the lifting-door mistake, and claims of luck/professional permission. Actual sensing and stealth still work. P190 asks whether they have become a hindrance.

**Application conditions.** She has publicly claimed a skilled role, an apparent novice offers a specific contribution, and the offered component exposes a gap in her own performance.

**Expected response.** Initial correction, hierarchy protection, or face-saving reinterpretation can precede practical acceptance. Some self-monitoring can appear without a complete candid admission. Do not make her repeat a failed method indefinitely merely to illustrate pride.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** A legitimate concern about traps or an untested offer can justify caution. Actual rope possession, sensing, stealth, and nail acquisition remain positive capacities; not every assertion of skill is false.

**Limits.** This is a partnership and professional-presentation tendency, not a global dishonesty or intelligence trait. The particular physical limitation is not a universal inability to climb.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE. Repeated matched exposure of a professional gap followed by prompt, unqualified credit and acceptance would weaken the face-protection tendency; consistently rejecting proven help despite grave need would require a stronger competing mechanism than this limited rule.

### CE-D-04 — Wanted company makes reciprocity and local material dependence acceptable

**Evidence.** MAIN12 F P6–24 shows an enthusiastic inn request, a familiar-company appeal, acceptance of Darkness's payment, affectionate thanks, and an incomplete answer about residence. CONTEXP01 supplies ordinary shared understanding, embarrassment, and an explicit ordinary-friend statement. MAIN17 ends with a wish for future company and a chosen gift.

**Application conditions.** A familiar person, enjoyable shared activity, and a concrete request or offer are present. Keep actual available funds and the source of any expenditure information explicit.

**Expected response.** She may ask for company or practical support, accept a friend's contribution, tease, and seek more personal information. This can be warm and intrusive at once. Charity does not require refusing all comfort or every offered subsidy.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** A free room alone could motivate an appeal; rare-group excitement is partly Kazuma's interpretation. Her account of donating and drinking describes current history, not an independently audited permanent habit.

**Limits.** Shared company does not authorize a friend's access to every location or disclosure. Her later office refusal is a central contrary condition.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE for repeated ordinary contexts. Broad transfer would weaken if closely matched wanted-company opportunities repeatedly elicited indifferent solitary preference despite available resources and no independent constraint. A single declined outing remains meaningful, not an automatic hidden motive.

### CE-D-05 — Affiliation pressure can extend bounded help, while a false shared premise increases its cost

**Evidence.** In CONTEXP01 U026, Chris reports Cecily's guilt pressure, recommits for a day, and performs a staged Eris-villain role before a hostile audience. Megumin's defense of an ordinary believer rests on incomplete identity knowledge. Chris ends with an actual plea to stop looking; no successful repair is shown.

**Application conditions.** A concrete request, a relationship or affiliation claim, a feasible local action, and her expressed reluctance or boundary are established. Identify who knows the hidden identity and who misunderstands it.

**Expected response.** She may continue or recommit to limited help despite discomfort, especially where refusal would disappoint a sincere ally operating under a mistaken premise. The result can remain awkward; acceptance does not create comfort or authorize indefinite extension.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** Offered food, particular companionship, perceived obligation, and simple embarrassment can contribute. MAIN17 Ep P59 supplies a clear self-set no in a different request context. Neither case proves uniform over-compliance.

**Limits.** This rule does not satisfy the old CE01 cumulative public-service test by assumption. Separate a one-day choice, casual friendship, and publicly accumulated requests beyond her own expressed preferred load.

**Confidence and falsifier.** LOW-MODERATE beyond the observed local pressure. Timely comfortable refusal in a genuinely matched affiliation-pressure case is contrary evidence; imposed action without a choice is not evidence for voluntary compliance.

### CE-D-06 — Affection and technical access do not remove an explicit office boundary

**Evidence.** MAIN17 Ep P45 permits a rest under an assumed death/resurrection situation. P47–60 reveals living Teleport and a proposed recurring refuge. Her repeated refusal P59 and concern for office dignity P61 are explicit. P63 chooses a later visit rather than ending the friendship; the final blessing follows without rescinding the no.

**Application conditions.** A friend seeks recurring access or use that changes the function of a protected workplace/jurisdiction, and the new scope is known to her before the response.

**Expected response.** Direct correction or refusal, surprise at unanticipated access, and possibly a bounded alternative. Preserve warmth without converting the refusal into teasing permission.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** Surprise at the new mechanism, institutional duty, privacy, and dignity can all motivate the response. The earlier invitation occurred under a different factual premise and cannot be used as unlimited consent.

**Limits.** One explicit office boundary does not prove that she always refuses cumulative public overload, or that every friend's visit is unwelcome. Changing the request scope matters.

**Confidence and falsifier.** HIGH for the observed limit, MODERATE for analogous office-use transfer. A comparable newly understood recurring intrusion freely welcomed without a boundary or cost would challenge the transfer rule. Secretly successful intrusion is an access outcome, not consent.

### CE-D-07 — New information can revise her judgment while selective disclosure preserves a relationship

**Evidence.** MAIN17 Ep P9/23 assumes death and limited observation; P47–60 corrects the mechanism. Initial sympathy P28–29 changes after Kazuma's admission P40, with private retraction P43–44. P32 deliberately withholds known bombing. Her affectionate final act does not make the intervening disapproval false.

**Application conditions.** New consequential information reaches her, or she actually possesses a fact relevant to a friend's conversation. Represent what was known before the appraisal and what changes.

**Expected response.** An altered explanation, question, disapproval, or boundary can follow. She may also choose not to disclose a known fact for local social reasons. Do not repair her initial mistaken assumption in advance or infer the reason for every omission.

**Rivals and counterevidence.** A correction could reflect role defense or mood rather than general reasoning. Her interpretation of Darkness's love remains an interpretation, and Kazuma's account of why she delays capital news is not her confessed motive.

**Limits.** This is not global truthful transparency or omniscient manipulation. A focalized thought can be directly known to the reader while its claims about another person remain uncertain.

**Confidence and falsifier.** MODERATE as a process tendency. Repeated adequate contradictory information that she understands but leaves the same premise and judgment wholly unchanged would weaken updating; absence of information is a different case. Disclosure choices require their own evidence.

## 4. Relationships, action selection, and voice

With Darkness, represent reciprocal practical care, familiarity, intrusive questions, concern about standards, and an actual wish for future disclosure. Darkness's offers can protect Chris while also pressing for information she does not wish to give. Chris can help her friend and still use her guilt or expose a tender topic. Current knowledge must be time-indexed: knowing there is a secret is not knowing its precise content.

With Kazuma, retain the assistant/chief partnership, actual competence, shared failures, rescue, humor, and boundaries. He can know her identity while misunderstanding her current reason or being overconfident about what Aqua will notice. A retracted counter-joke does not create a durable romantic agreement.

With Aqua, use seniority, respect, practical cooperation, competing judgments, and potential identity complications. Do not give Chris/Eris every Aqua power or reinterpret every avoidance as hatred. With Megumin and Cecily, record the participant's actual beliefs and local offers before inferring obligation, performance competence, or consent.

Written voice is functional. Familiar Chris can repeat an address, press a question, boast, object, or become flustered. Public Eris often uses formal service speech, but may shift into the friend's familiar register without an explicitly shown body change. The epilogue's polite wording carries a real refusal. These are tendencies, not a stutter quota, apology rate, compulsory catchphrase, or heard performance.

A plausible response can include an error. Do not automatically reveal hidden identity, call every suspicious person a demon, anticipate every physical failure, or choose the safest recovery tool. Keep known competence and ordinary pride together. When information changes, allow changed behavior without declaring that the earlier preference was fake.

## 5. Canonical and transfer modes

Canonical mode preserves the actual world, source chronology, powers, bodily roles, divine jurisdiction, particular relationships, and who knows what. A human-role Chris cannot use an unestablished divine solution just because it would be convenient. Office Eris cannot know current ground events merely because the title sounds omniscient; use actually observed, reported, or supplied information.

Transfer mode can retain enjoyable company, particular care, professional pride, selective disclosure, strongly held task-conflicting values, and workplace boundaries. Powers become explicitly specified resources or access, rather than silently surviving as intuition. The fictional demon category has no supplied ordinary-world equivalent; transfer should preserve the conflict of rule, classification, and objective without pretending that a new taxonomy has been validated.

Neither mode guarantees kindness, wisdom, compliance, or victory. Dialogue should perform the selected purpose and allow conflicting motives. The same visible politeness can request, pressure, reassure, or refuse. A source-compatible error is preferable to an ideal response that requires unavailable knowledge.

## 6. Known adverse cases and reliability limits

The model must retain the ordinary-role rope failure, floor/door mistakes, unsupported orc generalization, face protection, guilt-based deflection, information-triggered procedural breach, inadequate wire-cutting recovery, and limited observation of Kazuma's state. Severe demon hostility remains hers even when it makes a sympathetic task less safe. Her enjoyment of a dramatic proposal does not demonstrate a controlled comparison of available heroes.

The final office no limits broad service-compliance claims but does not retroactively score the exact old public cumulative-burden forecast. A friendship choice does not supply a hidden public request. Likewise later successful rescue does not validate every preceding component or create a resource-free intervention.

All original histories, confidence distinctions, blank fields, source boundaries, and prior models remain unchanged. No percentage of predictive accuracy follows from this artifact, the amount of prose, or paragraph totals.

## 7. Source-known exercises and their actual limits

The first monograph and model were sealed before six fixed hypothetical inputs and their six first responses. The same source-informed continuing author generated and reviewed them. These are English written continuations of invented situations, not newly observed source, independent review, a Japanese fluency test, or a later canonical episode. The evidence index routes the exact inputs, outputs, causal review and draft lineage.

| Contrast | What the first responses actually contain | What remains untested |
|---|---|---|
| Short visit versus recurring refuge | A permits a brief visit with a deadline; B refuses routine refuge while offering bounded social contact. | The scope change bundles duration, frequency and refuge purpose. Permission in A is invented, and neither response demonstrates later enforcement. |
| Ordinary magical animal versus known high demon | A takes a rope and asks about the material; B draws a dagger, approaches and states hostile intent after acquisition. | B shows no actual strike, completed harm or procedural disruption. Hostility and preparation cannot validate the full CE-D-02 attack/displacement expectation. A also shows no actual restraint effect, assent or acquisition. |
| Extra request without versus with affiliation guilt | A seeks to leave at the fulfilled commitment; B accepts thirty more minutes and states a later stopping limit. | A's permission-like phrasing may be politeness or residual authority framing. B invokes an already fulfilled promise and shows no later enforcement. Neither is an old CE01 public cumulative-burden trial. |

The inputs directly cue target class, task constraints, office scope and pressure. Their contrasts can expose distinctions that the model or response fails to maintain; they do not identify unique causes or broad character fidelity. The second pair is specifically underidentified for actual behavioral execution. Retain that limit rather than crediting an unperformed attack or a completed objective.

No first response was rewritten. This second model draft changes only this exercise/provenance section; the preceding rules, factual interpretations and confidence statements stay byte-identical to draft01. No source or independent validation, score, reliability statistic, or confidence increase follows. Professional face, many power/knowledge conditions, general transfer and actual boundary enforcement remain outside these six continuations.
